topic: Google DeepMind open-sources WeatherNext Cyclones after a Nature paper shows +24h average extra cyclone warning lead time
primary_source_note: All claims verified against primary sources read in full: (1) DeepMind blog 'WeatherNext: AI model achieves breakthrough in forecasting cyclones' (Aug 6 2026), (2) Nature paper s41586-026-10953-2 'Operational Tropical Cyclone Forecasting with AI' (published Aug 6 2026), (3) DeepMind Melissa post (May 19 2026), (4) NHC 2025 Verification Report PDF (Mar 30 2026, 85pp - downloaded and text-read), (5) blog.google coverage (Aug 6 2026), (6) developers.google.com/weathernext. Gemini Spark's '97.2%/99.8% accuracy' and '50-100+ scenarios' figures were NOT found in any primary source and are DROPPED - the real ensemble count is 1,000 (was 50 in 2025).

source.published: Aug 6 2026 (blog + Nature paper); NHC report Mar 30 2026

claims.claim: WeatherNext gives forecasters an extra day of predictive accuracy on average: its 3-day forecasts match what prior models gave at 2 days
Average lead-time advantage is more than a full day (24 hours) for track, intensity and wind structure, benchmarked on historical cyclones 2023-2024
Improvement is roughly a decade of meteorological progress - 3-day accuracy equivalent to 20-year trend lines for ECMWF-ENS track and HWRF intensity
Model predicts global weather + cyclone tracks up to 15 days ahead, as a 1,000-member ensemble, producing localized probability maps of tropical-storm to hurricane-force winds
A single 15-day forecast generates in under a minute on a TPU; ensemble scaled from 50 (2025) to 1,000 members to capture rare rapid-intensification scenarios
Trains on ~20 TB of global atmospheric data plus the IBTrACS historical storm database (~5,000 storms)

Only needs 28x28 km inputs - roughly 100x coarser than traditional high-res models; a 111x111 km mini version (WeatherNext 2-mini) also performs well; scientists call why-it-works an open research question
Tropical cyclones caused more than 700,000 deaths and $1.4 trillion in economic losses globally over the past 50 years
Paper 'Operational Tropical Cyclone Forecasting with AI' published in Nature Aug 6 2026 (s41586-026-10953-2)
During the 2025 hurricane season WeatherNext ran operationally alongside the NHC and helped with Hurricane Melissa's historic forecast
Hurricane Melissa (Oct 2025) was the strongest hurricane on record to land in Jamaica and tied for the strongest ever in the Atlantic
NHC predicted Melissa would reach Category 5 starting from Category 1 wind speed - a first - and WeatherNext flagged Cat-5 landfall in Jamaica 5 days out at 80% confidence, near 100% 3 days out

NHC's own 2025 Verification Report (Mar 30 2026): the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly outperformed NHC official track forecasts at 12-72h and was best-of-class at 96-120h; best individual intensity model; in the eastern Pacific it beat the official forecast and all consensus aids at 48-120h
Open-sourced Aug 6 2026: WeatherNext 2, WeatherNext Cyclones and WeatherNext 2-mini (single TPU, free public Colab); forecast data queryable via BigQuery and Earth Engine

Honest gap: official warnings still come from human forecasters at national agencies - the blog states 'For official weather forecasts and warnings, refer to your local meteorological agency' - WeatherNext is decision support, and 1,000-member runs need a TPU-class machine
NHC serves ~30 countries as WMO Regional Specialized Meteorological Center; DeepMind is partnering with agencies in the Philippines (PAGASA), Taiwan (CWA), Indonesia (BMKG), Vietnam (VNMHA)
